title: CLR/127/1994 of SURENDRA BHADRI Vs YATAYAT EVAM FRAYATAN /SAHKARI SANGH

paras.text:
Court No.2
Civil Revision No. 412 of 2001
 (Old No. 127/1994)
Surendra Bhadri ............. Plaintiff/
Revisionist.
Versus
Yatayat Evam Prayatan
Vikas Sahkari Sangh Ltd.
and two others. .........Defendants/
 Respondents.
Hon'ble P.C.Verma, J.
This revision has been filed by the
Plaintiff/revisionist challenging the order dated
20.8.1993 passed by the then District Judge, Tehri
Garhwal, rejecting the application 82-A filed in
Suit No. 40 of 1989 for amendment in the plaint
for deletion of cetian land from the suit land
and order dated 07.2.1994 passed on the application
for recall of order dated 20.8.1993.
The reasons recorded by the learned
District Judge for rejecting the application are
that the said amdnement application was moved
when the case property stood poised for finalization
after settlement of issues and he further gave the
following reasons:-
"if certain property is deleted,
There would be fresh suit brought against that
deleted property. In such a situation then,
when court fee about that property sought
to be deleted stands already paid and the
controversy is complicated one wherein
decision in respect of one part would
involve decision of other also, in my view,
this application for recall should not be
allowed. I, therefore, reject this application."
The reasons recorded as quoted above can
not be the reasons refusing to amend the plaint

where the deletion of certain land from the suit
was sought for. It is settled law that the amendment
can only be refused when it changes the nature of
the suit. In the present case, no finding has been
recorded that if amendment application is allowed
it will change the nature of the suit. Since the
amendment sought was only for the deletion of certain
land from the suit land, by allowing he amendment
nature of the plaint was not to be changed. Moreso,
it is the choice of the plaintiff to file a suit
for land against which he has a cause of action.
Deletion of the certain land shows that the plaintiff
has no cause of action for that he wanted to delete
the certain land from the suit land. Therefore,
the amendment was permissible under law. The orders
passed by the District Judge on 20.8.1993 and
07.2.1994 are hereby quashed. The amendment appli-Cation 82-A moved by the plaintiff in Original Suit
No.40 of 1989 is allowed.
The revision is allowed accordingly.
Since the suit is of year 1989, the
learned District Judge, Tehri Garhwal is directed
to conclude the hearing of the suit within a period
of six months from the date of production of
certified copy of this order.
(P.C.Verma, J.)
26.11.2001
P.Singh
